chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hajjal, from Thalabah, from Muhammad ibn Mudarib, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
There is no problem with selling the animal dung.

key_terms.الْعَذِرَةِ: Animal dung (specifically from cows or camels, used as fuel/fertilizer)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem/It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell animal dung in Islam?
ai.summary: This concise hadith from al-Kafi establishes the permissibility (jawaaz) of selling animal dung (ath-dhira), reflecting the practical economic realities of 9th-century Iraq where dried cow dung was a primary fuel source for heating and cooking. It underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that items possessing utility (manfa'ah) and not inherently impure (najis) in a way that prevents trade, are valid commodities, thereby validating everyday agricultural and domestic markets.
